VIDEO DATE: 2019-03-19
TRANSCRIPT EXCERPT: People who are vaccinated against chickenpox need to keep getting boosters.
CLAIM: People who are vaccinated against chickenpox need to keep getting boosters.
VERIFICATION QUESTIONS:
- How many booster shots are recommended after receiving the initial chickenpox vaccine?

EVIDENCE:
[1] https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2019/roll117.xml Yes
[2] https://historyofvaccines.org/diseases/chickenpox-varicella One.
The U.S. Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices recommends two doses of the chickenpox vaccine for most children. The first dose is given around age 1 and the second around ages 4-6. A single dose of the vaccine reduces the risk of chickenpox between 70-90%, and two doses reduce the risk even more.
The chickenpox vaccine was added to the childhood immunization schedule in 1995. The booster dose was added in 2006.
[3] https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/21/health/medicare-for-all-hospitals.html Big hospital systems haggle constantly with Medicare over what they are paid, and often battle the government over charges of overbilling. On average, the government program pays hospitals about 87 cents for every dollar of their costs, compared with private insurers that pay $1.45.

VIDEO DATE: 2020-07-21
TRANSCRIPT EXCERPT: A study finds a diet heavy with kimchi—spiced fermented cabbage and other vegetables—helps lower South Korea's COVID-19 fatalities.
CLAIM: A study finds a diet heavy with kimchi—spiced fermented cabbage and other vegetables—helps lower South Korea's COVID-19 fatalities.
VERIFICATION QUESTIONS:
- Has eating kimchi, spicy fermented cabbage, and other vegetables helped lower COVID-19 fatalities in Korea?
- Has there been a study on the consumption of fermented vegetables and COVID-19 mortality?
- Is Korea mentioned in the study on the consumption of fermented vegetables and COVID-19 mortality report?
- Could the study be extrapolated to Korea?
- Can this study be relied upon?
NUMBER CHECK (deterministic):
- claim says 19; nearest evidence figure 9 in [1] (different)

EVIDENCE:

It found that students reported lower levels of anxiety when surveyed in April and May of this year compared to October 2019. 

It also found an increase in wellbeing but “no large change in risk of depression.”

These passengers – Red Cross staff – arrived ready to “carry out their duties and keep high the spirits of Yank fighting men.”

VIDEO DATE: unknown
TRANSCRIPT EXCERPT: There is pork in Covid-19 vaccines.
CLAIM: There is pork in Covid-19 vaccines.
VERIFICATION QUESTIONS:
- What is covid-19 vaccine made of
NUMBER CHECK (deterministic):
- claim says 19; nearest evidence figure 11 in [4] (different)

EVIDENCE:
[1] https://practio.co.uk/coronavirus/articles/coronavirus-vaccine-ingredients The active substance is BNT162b2 RNA, lipids, salts, sugar and water
[2] https://web.archive.org/web/20210705182533/https://fas.org/sgp/crs/misc//RL32013.pdf If a negative blue slip is received, the chairman may take the following actions
on the nominee: (1) stop all committee proceedings; (2) move forward but give added
weight to the unfavorable review; or (3) proceed without notice of the negative
review. Since the late 1970s, the committee has generally used the latter two actions
when dealing with a negative blue slip
[3] https://nasa.tumblr.com/post/150688852794/zodiac?linkId=94146490 Here at NASA, we study astronomy, not astrology. We didn’t change any zodiac signs, we just did the math.
[4] https://web.archive.org/web/20210608110450/http://vk.ovg.ox.ac.uk/vaccine-ingredients#thiomersal Thiomersal was removed from UK vaccines between 2003 and 2005, and is no longer found in any of the childhood or adult vaccines routinely used in the UK. Before 2005, thiomersal was present in diphtheria- and tetanus-containing vaccines, as well as hepatitis B vaccine and some flu vaccines. It was not used in the MMR vaccine, the Hib vaccine, the MenC vaccine, the oral polio vaccine or the BCG vaccine. Thiomersal was present in the Swine Flu (H1N1) vaccine Pandemrix, used in the 2009-10 and 2010-11 flu seasons in the UK. However, it is not present in any of the annual flu vaccines currently in use in the UK.

Before the Affordable Care Act, Congress and staffers got their health care through employer-provided insurance, the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program. During the ACA debate, the idea that members of Congress would not be subject to the exchanges became a big political issue. So, the final "ACA" (Obamacare) required lawmakers and staffers to get their insurance through the local health exchange, the District of Columbia’s small business health options program (SHOP) exchange.

For the 2017 plan year, there were 57 plan options in the gold tier on the DC SHOP. Members and staff have to choose at least the gold option to receive the employer contribution, which is figured at 72% of the weighted average of all FEHB plan premiums.

As humans have spread across the world, so have infectious diseases. Even in this modern era, outbreaks are nearly constant, though not every outbreak reaches pandemic level as COVID-19 has.

The History of Pandemics

Pan·dem·ic /panˈdemik/ (of a disease) prevalent over a whole country or the world.

As humans have spread across the world, so have infectious diseases. Even in this modern era, outbreaks are nearly constant, though not every outbreak reaches pandemic level as COVID-19 has.

Today’s visualization outlines some of history’s most deadly pandemics, from the Antonine Plague to the current COVID-19 event.
A Timeline of Historical Pandemics
